name: Question 2
problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=3{x}_{1}(t)-4{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=2{x}_{1}(t)+6{x}_{2}(t),\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform to both sides of each equation, we get the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{{field-1}}={{field-2}} \\ {{field-3}}=2{X}_{1}(s)+6{X}_{2}(s)\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L{{x}_{2}(t)}$ are the Laplace transforms of the functions ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t),$ respectively.
worked_solution:
First, we find the Laplace transforms of both sides of each equation in our system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}L{{x}_{1}^{′}(t)}=L{3{x}_{1}(t)-4{x}_{2}(t)} \\ L{{x}_{2}^{′}(t)}=L{2{x}_{1}(t)+6{x}_{2}(t)}\end{aligned}\,\,
$$

Using the derivative property of the Laplace transform, we obtain the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}sL{{x}_{1}(t)}-{x}_{1}(0)=3L{{x}_{1}(t)}-4L{{x}_{2}(t)} \\ sL{{x}_{2}(t)}-{x}_{2}(0)=2L{{x}_{1}(t)}+6L{{x}_{2}(t)}\end{aligned}
$$

which can be simplified to the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)+2=3{X}_{1}(s)-4{X}_{2}(s) \\ s{X}_{2}(s)-5=2{X}_{1}(s)+6{X}_{2}(s)\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L{{x}_{2}(t)}$ are the Laplace transforms of the functions ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t),$ respectively.
